title: Boyhood friends and Edison records of George Hamilton Green
summary: No radio; the family had thick Edison records of Ray Miller's orchestra and xylophonist George Hamilton Green, and he met other musicians such as Frank Skinner and Mel Hewlett as he got older.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: Did you have many pals around? Kids your own age, convenient?

As I got a little older I met some. Course there was Mel Healt who was in that town and the Skinner boys, you know Frank Skinner. They -- he had the Ranger, he had three brothers that worked in Macedosia, which is right down the River a little ways --
And they used to come up all the time.
Did you -- didn't have radio, but what about phonograph. Did they have phonographs?
Well did your family have any records?
Yeah, but -- yeah, but I mean --
But what were you listening to on them?
Yeah, when I came back I found out that he made Victor -- made Edison records.
Yeah. I had -- I got them --
-- I used to listen to them.
And he had an all-star trio. On Victor, too. You had a gadget where you could play the Edison and also the other kind, play the small kind, you know --
It was different you needed a diamond point needle or something or other.
I don't remember too much about it.
Yeah, but that's how it was. Yeah.
Yeah. Well anyway, so then you let the pony go --
